chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'When you sit in the first two rak'at, so you perform the Tashahhud, then stand, so say, 'By the Might of Allah and His Strength I am standing and sitting'.'
ai.seo_question: What supplication should be recited when standing up from the first two rak'at in prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific dhikr to be recited upon rising from the first two rak'at, emphasizing reliance on Allah's power (quwwah) and sustenance (quwwah) for physical movement. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating conscious remembrance with ritual actions, transforming mechanical movements into acts of spiritual awareness. The phrase highlights the theological concept that all human capability is derived from divine enablement, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence and spirituality.
